유행이 되었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 최근 과학철학에서는. <break time="0.8s" /> 특정 종류의 모형을 이상화된 모형이라고 부르는 것이. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 이른바 이상화를 나누는 것이. <break time="0.8s" /> 아리스토텔레스식 이상화와 갈릴레오식 이상화로. <break time="0.8s" /> 이 설명에 따르면, 아리스토텔레스식 이상화는 이루어진다 상상 속에서 벗겨 내는 것으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 구체적인 대상에서 모든 속성을. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 우리가 관련이 없다고 믿는 속성들이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 당면한 문제와 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 이것은 우리가 집중할 수 있게 해 준다. <break time="0.8s" /> 따로 떼어 낸 제한된 일련의 속성에. <break time="0.8s" /> 한 가지 예는 행성계의 고전역학 모형인데. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것은 행성을 물체로 기술한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 모양과 질량만 가진 물체로. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 다른 모든 속성은 무시한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 반면에, 갈릴레오식 이상화는. <break time="0.8s" /> 의도적인 왜곡을 수반하는 것이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 물리학자는 모형을 만든다. <break time="0.8s" /> 점질량으로 이루어진 모형을. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 점질량은 마찰 없는 면 위를 움직인다. <break time="0.8s" /> 경제학자는 경제 주체가 전지전능하다고 가정한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 생물학자는 고립된 개체군을 연구하는 식이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 과학에 대한 갈릴레오의 접근 방식의 특징이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 이런 종류의 단순화를 사용하는 것이. <break time="0.8s" /> 상황이 너무 복잡해서 다룰 수 없을 때마다.

It has become popular in recent philosophy of science to call certain kinds of models idealized models, and to divide so called idealization into Aristotelian idealization and Galilean idealization. <break time="0.8s" /> On this account, Aristotelian idealization consists of stripping away, in our imagination, all properties from a concrete object that we believe are not relevant to the problem at hand. <break time="0.8s" /> This allows us to focus on a limited set of properties in isolation. <break time="0.8s" /> An example is a classical mechanics model of the planetary system, which describes the planets as objects only having shape and mass and disregards all other properties. <break time="0.8s" /> Galilean idealizations, on the other hand, are ones that involve deliberate distortions. <break time="0.8s" /> Physicists build models consisting of point masses moving on frictionless planes, economists assume that agents are omniscient, biologists study isolated populations, and so on. <break time="0.8s" /> It was characteristic of Galileos approach to science to use simplifications of this sort whenever a situation was too complicated to tackle.

All causal sequences share one thing in common. <break time="0.8s" /> That is missing in all coincidental sequences. <break time="0.8s" /> They are instances of, they instantiate, general laws. <break time="0.8s" /> This philosophical theory, which owes its origins. <break time="0.8s" /> To the eighteenth century empiricist philosopher David Hume. <break time="0.8s" /> Does not require, for every causal claim we make. <break time="0.8s" /> That we already know the law or laws. <break time="0.8s" /> Which connect the cause and effect. <break time="0.8s" /> Children will explain, correctly we suppose. <break time="0.8s" /> Why the vase broke. <break time="0.8s" /> By admitting that it was dropped. <break time="0.8s" /> Passive voice, silence on who dropped it. <break time="0.8s" /> On a marble floor. <break time="0.8s" /> We accept the statement. <break time="0.8s" /> As identifying the cause. <break time="0.8s" /> Even though neither the children nor we know. <break time="0.8s" /> The relevant laws. <break time="0.8s" /> Humes theory does not require. <break time="0.8s" /> That we do so. <break time="0.8s" /> It only requires. <break time="0.8s" /> That there is a law or laws. <break time="0.8s" /> Already known or not yet discovered, which do so. <break time="0.8s" /> The task of science is to uncover these laws. <break time="0.8s" /> And to employ them in explanations of effects.

모든 인과적 연쇄는 한 가지를 공통으로 지닌다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것은 모든 우연적 연쇄에는 없는 것이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 그것들은 일반 법칙의 사례이다, 법칙을 구체적으로 보여 준다. <break time="0.8s" /> 이 철학 이론은, 그 기원이. <break time="0.8s" /> 18세기 경험주의 철학자 David Hume에게 있는데. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리가 하는 모든 인과 주장에 대해 요구하지는 않는다. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리가 법칙이나 법칙들을 이미 알고 있을 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 원인과 결과를 연결하는 법칙 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 아이들은 설명할 것이다, 우리가 생각하기에 올바르게. <break time="0.8s" /> 꽃병이 왜 깨졌는지를. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것이 떨어뜨려졌다고 인정함으로써. <break time="0.8s" /> 수동태로, 누가 떨어뜨렸는지는 말하지 않고. <break time="0.8s" /> 대리석 바닥에 떨어뜨려졌다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리는 그 진술을 받아들인다. <break time="0.8s" /> 원인을 밝히는 것으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 아이들도 우리도 알지 못하는데도. <break time="0.8s" /> 관련 법칙을 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> Hume의 이론은 요구하지 않는다. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리가 그렇게 할 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것은 다만 요구한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 법칙이나 법칙들이 존재할 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 이미 알려졌든 아직 발견되지 않았든, 그렇게 하는 법칙 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 과학의 과제는 이러한 법칙을 밝혀내는 것이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그것들을 결과에 대한 설명에 사용하는 것이다.

All causal sequences share one thing in common that is missing in all coincidental sequences, they are instances of, they instantiate, general laws. <break time="0.8s" /> This philosophical theory, which owes its origins to the eighteenth century empiricist philosopher David Hume, does not require, for every causal claim we make, that we already know the law or laws which connect the cause and effect. <break time="0.8s" /> Children will explain, correctly we suppose, why the vase broke, by admitting that it was dropped passive voice, silence on who dropped it, on a marble floor. <break time="0.8s" /> We accept the statement as identifying the cause, even though neither the children nor we know the relevant laws. <break time="0.8s" /> Humes theory does not require that we do so. <break time="0.8s" /> It only requires that there is a law or laws, already known or not yet discovered, which do so. <break time="0.8s" /> The task of science is to uncover these laws, and to employ them in explanations of effects.

Almost every day we find ourselves in situations. <break time="0.8s" /> In which we apply, consciously or unconsciously. <break time="0.8s" /> Mathematical knowledge. <break time="0.8s" /> Basic abilities in arithmetic are among those mathematical competencies. <break time="0.8s" /> We use most frequently. <break time="0.8s" /> We may estimate the time we need. <break time="0.8s" /> To get from one place to another. <break time="0.8s" /> Combining different means of transportation. <break time="0.8s" /> Or calculate the total cost of the products in our shopping cart. <break time="0.8s" /> Before we go to the register. <break time="0.8s" /> Of course, one could argue. <break time="0.8s" /> That mastering arithmetic is nowadays unnecessary and old fashioned. <break time="0.8s" /> Since the cellphone practically everybody carries around. <break time="0.8s" /> Is a smartphone. <break time="0.8s" /> Which can be used as a calculator. <break time="0.8s" /> However, simple calculations can often be done. <break time="0.8s" /> Much faster without the assistance of a calculator. <break time="0.8s" /> It also keeps the brain fit. <break time="0.8s" /> And using our own built in computer. <break time="0.8s" /> Is definitely more enjoyable. <break time="0.8s" /> Than commanding an electronic device. <break time="0.8s" /> But, most important, arithmetic offers an accessible playground. <break time="0.8s" /> For everyone to learn and develop. <break time="0.8s" /> Mathematical thinking and problem solving strategies. <break time="0.8s" /> Which can, in fact, be very helpful. <break time="0.8s" /> For making decisions in our everyday lives.

거의 매일 우리는 상황에 놓이게 된다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 상황에서 우리는 의식적으로든 무의식적으로든 적용한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 수학 지식을. <break time="0.8s" /> 기본적인 산수 능력은 그 수학적 역량들 중 하나이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리가 가장 자주 사용하는 역량 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리는 필요한 시간을 어림할 수도 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 한 장소에서 다른 장소로 가는 데. <break time="0.8s" /> 서로 다른 교통수단을 조합하면서. <break time="0.8s" /> 또는 장바구니에 담긴 상품들의 총액을 계산할 수도 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 계산대에 가기 전에. <break time="0.8s" /> 물론, 누군가는 주장할 수도 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 산수를 숙달하는 것은 오늘날 불필요하고 구식이라고. <break time="0.8s" /> 거의 모든 사람이 들고 다니는 휴대전화가. <break time="0.8s" /> 스마트폰이기 때문에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것은 계산기로 쓰일 수 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러나, 간단한 계산은 이루어질 수 있는 경우가 많다. <break time="0.8s" /> 계산기의 도움 없이 훨씬 더 빨리. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것은 또한 두뇌를 건강하게 유지해 주며. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 우리 자신의 내장된 컴퓨터를 사용하는 것은. <break time="0.8s" /> 확실히 더 즐겁다. <break time="0.8s" /> 전자 기기를 조작하는 것보다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만, 가장 중요하게는, 산수는 접근 가능한 놀이터를 제공한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 모든 사람이 배우고 발전시킬 수 있도록. <break time="0.8s" /> 수학적 사고와 문제 해결 전략을. <break time="0.8s" /> 이것은 사실 매우 도움이 될 수 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리의 일상생활에서 결정을 내리는 데.

Almost every day we find ourselves in situations in which we apply, consciously or unconsciously, mathematical knowledge. <break time="0.8s" /> Basic abilities in arithmetic are among those mathematical competencies we use most frequently. <break time="0.8s" /> We may estimate the time we need to get from one place to another, combining different means of transportation, or calculate the total cost of the products in our shopping cart before we go to the register. <break time="0.8s" /> Of course, one could argue that mastering arithmetic is nowadays unnecessary and old fashioned, since the cellphone practically everybody carries around is a smartphone, which can be used as a calculator. <break time="0.8s" /> However, simple calculations can often be done much faster without the assistance of a calculator. <break time="0.8s" /> It also keeps the brain fit, and using our own built in computer is definitely more enjoyable than commanding an electronic device. <break time="0.8s" /> But, most important, arithmetic offers an accessible playground for everyone to learn and develop mathematical thinking and problem solving strategies, which can, in fact, be very helpful for making decisions in our everyday lives.

In the academic world, scholars have long debated. <break time="0.8s" /> The intentions behind Socrates assertions of ignorance. <break time="0.8s" /> In Platos dialogues. <break time="0.8s" /> We have no way to distinguish the instances. <break time="0.8s" /> In which Plato intended Socrates to be purposefully deceptive. <break time="0.8s" /> From those in which his claims of ignorance were genuine. <break time="0.8s" /> In addition, there has been an extended discussion. <break time="0.8s" /> About what Plato and Aristotle intended. <break time="0.8s" /> By using the term eiron. <break time="0.8s" /> Melissa Lane has observed that in Aristophanes time. <break time="0.8s" /> The word meant one who feigns ignorance. <break time="0.8s" /> Which clearly points to deliberate pretense or deception. <break time="0.8s" /> About sixty five years after Aristophanes. <break time="0.8s" /> Aristotle uses the same term. <break time="0.8s" /> To refer to humble self deprecation. <break time="0.8s" /> So was Plato, writing in between these two eras. <break time="0.8s" /> Using the word in its earlier sense. <break time="0.8s" /> Or was he anticipating or creating the later meaning. <break time="0.8s" /> Gregory Vlastos asserts that Platos Socrates did not intend to deceive. <break time="0.8s" /> And that we should view him instead. <break time="0.8s" /> As providing his interlocutors with enlightenment and instruction.

학계에서는, 학자들이 오랫동안 논쟁해 왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 소크라테스의 무지 주장 뒤에 숨은 의도를. <break time="0.8s" /> 플라톤의 대화편에 나오는 주장 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리는 두 가지 경우를 구별할 방법이 없다. <break time="0.8s" /> 플라톤이 소크라테스를 일부러 남을 속이는 인물로 그린 경우와. <break time="0.8s" /> 소크라테스가 모른다고 한 말이 진심이었던 경우를. <break time="0.8s" /> 게다가, 긴 논의가 있어 왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 플라톤과 아리스토텔레스가 무엇을 의도했는지에 대한. <break time="0.8s" /> Eiron이라는 용어를 사용함으로써. <break time="0.8s" /> Melissa Lane은 아리스토파네스 시대에 다음과 같았다고 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 단어는 무지한 척하는 사람을 의미했다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 이는 분명히 의도적인 가장이나 기만을 가리킨다. <break time="0.8s" /> 아리스토파네스보다 약 65년 뒤에. <break time="0.8s" /> 아리스토텔레스는 같은 용어를 사용한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 겸손한 자기 비하를 가리키는 데. <break time="0.8s" /> 그렇다면 이 두 시대 사이에 글을 쓴 플라톤은. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 단어를 이전의 의미로 사용하고 있었던 것일까. <break time="0.8s" /> 아니면 그는 이후의 의미를 예견하고 또는 만들어 내고 있었던 것일까. <break time="0.8s" /> Gregory Vlastos는 플라톤의 소크라테스가 속이려고 의도한 것이 아니라고 주장한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 우리는 오히려 그를 다음과 같은 사람으로 보아야 한다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 대화 상대에게 깨달음과 가르침을 주는 사람으로.

In the academic world, scholars have long debated the intentions behind Socrates assertions of ignorance in Platos dialogues. <break time="0.8s" /> We have no way to distinguish the instances in which Plato intended Socrates to be purposefully deceptive from those in which his claims of ignorance were genuine. <break time="0.8s" /> In addition, there has been an extended discussion about what Plato and Aristotle intended by using the term eiron. <break time="0.8s" /> Melissa Lane has observed that in Aristophanes time, the word meant one who feigns ignorance, which clearly points to deliberate pretense or deception. <break time="0.8s" /> About sixty five years after Aristophanes, Aristotle uses the same term to refer to humble self deprecation. <break time="0.8s" /> So was Plato, writing in between these two eras, using the word in its earlier sense, or was he anticipating or creating the later meaning. <break time="0.8s" /> Gregory Vlastos asserts that Platos Socrates did not intend to deceive, and that we should view him instead as providing his interlocutors with enlightenment and instruction.

The behavioral changes that occur within the parent adolescent relationship. <break time="0.8s" /> Primarily involve the development of a new balance. <break time="0.8s" /> Between attachment behaviors. <break time="0.8s" /> And the adolescents needs for autonomous exploration. <break time="0.8s" /> Adolescents are increasingly able to make their own choices. <break time="0.8s" /> And to regulate their own behaviors. <break time="0.8s" /> And they do so more and more frequently. <break time="0.8s" /> Without their parents watchful eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> Indeed, this increased self regulation is often sanctioned by parents. <break time="0.8s" /> Generally speaking, increasing maturity implies increased safety. <break time="0.8s" /> Which reduces the need for constant vigilance. <break time="0.8s" /> On the part of parents. <break time="0.8s" /> However, this process does not always proceed. <break time="0.8s" /> Completely smoothly. <break time="0.8s" /> As evidenced by heightened conflicts. <break time="0.8s" /> And increases in rates of lying and disobedience. <break time="0.8s" /> The good news perhaps not for parents is that these perturbations in the ways that teens behave with parents. <break time="0.8s" /> Are normative. <break time="0.8s" /> And equilibrium tends to be regained by early adulthood. <break time="0.8s" /> For example, as adolescents get older. <break time="0.8s" /> Teens become once again less likely to lie to their parents. <break time="0.8s" /> And more likely to disclose information. <break time="0.8s" /> About things that are important to them. <break time="0.8s" /> And parent teen conflict also decreases. <break time="0.8s" /> Said differently, this return to a more harmonious state. <break time="0.8s" /> Corresponds with the achievement of autonomy. <break time="0.8s" /> That is seen by early adulthood.

It is worth pointing out that leaves do not drop to the ground because they are dying, rather, the tree initiates an active process of clever recycling called senescence. <break time="0.8s" /> A tree, like an oak for example, would struggle to survive through a harsh winter if it retained its canopy of leaves. <break time="0.8s" /> It would risk damage from strong winter winds and would lose more water from its leaves than it could draw up from the frozen ground. <break time="0.8s" /> If it did not blow over, it would die of thirst. <break time="0.8s" /> As winter approaches, the length of the day shortens, the temperature drops, and plants, including trees, can detect this change. <break time="0.8s" /> It signals to them that it is time to lose their leaves. <break time="0.8s" /> First, however, trees carefully suck all of the useful nutrients out of the leaves and then, with surgical precision, block up that pathway into the leaves. <break time="0.8s" /> That blocked pathway at the base of the leaf stem creates a weakness and, in the wind, the leaves snap off and fall to the ground.
